overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the minutes complaint was untimely, the notice listing 'Bridge Street Sidewalks' was sufficiently specific, and no outside deliberation was shown. The DPW presentation point was not an OML allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the minutes of the September 9, 2014 Board meeting were inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: Because this was more than 30 days after the date of the approval of the minutes, we find the allegation regarding the minutes is untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged Board members deliberated outside a meeting about installing sidewalks along Bridge Street before the December 16, 2014 vote.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of any evidence to the contrary, we credit the Board members' assertions that there was no deliberation and find no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the December 16, 2014 notice listing 'Bridge Street Sidewalks' was not sufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Despite these expectations, because the notice informed the public that the Board would be considering a sidewalk along Bridge Street, and that is in fact what they discussed during the meeting, we find that it was sufficient to comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint about a Department of Public Works presentation at the Board meeting, which the AG said did not allege an Open Meeting Law violation.
allegations.key_passage: An additional allegation regarding a Chatham Department of Public Works presentation did not allege a violation of the Open Meeting Law.
